note: Published, not buried. Non-blocking by design: none of these stops the site or the merge. Each needs an owner decision or a source that does not exist yet.

flags.finding: Eight merged sessions each shipped a separate site tree at the repo root: `/`, `docs/`, `dashboard/`, `lab/`, `x3lab/`, `pages/`, `site/`, `legacy/`. Root `index.html` was a bare meta-refresh redirect to `lab/`, and each tree re-implements the same pages, so the same fact exists in 4-5 places with no canonical copy.
flags.evidence: https://github.com/karagemop466-tech/X3/tree/main - 180 tracked files, 9 index.html files, 4 injury pages, 5 suggestions pages
flags.impact: Decision-makers compare numbers from different snapshots and disagree; no single URL is citable
flags.action: Suggestion S-01: adopt this hub as canonical, demote the other trees to a labelled archive
flags.status: OPEN - hub published, archive page created, legacy trees left in place per no-delete policy

flags.finding: RETRAITED after cross-verification - the earlier reading of this flag was wrong. The official standings module does NOT lag the completed Thursday game. Reconciliation: summing the in-repo 2026 game log (SRC-17) over weeks 1-9 gives WAS 2-5-1 / 172-202 and NYG 5-2-1 / 182-172; adding the Week-10 Thursday final (WAS 24, NYG 21) gives exactly the WAS 3-5-1 / 196-223 and NYG 5-3-1 / 203-196 printed on the standings page and in the game page's own division widget. All 32 clubs reconcile on wins, losses, ties, points for and points against once LA->LAR and ARI->AZ are aliased. The 'standings are stale by one game' hypothesis came from this session's assumption that the page was a Week-9-only snapshot; it is not - it is 'all games through 2026-11-12'.
flags.impact: What survives is the weaker, still-important point: the standings page has no printed cut-off, so its as-of has to be inferred. An inferred as-of is how this flag was raised in error in the first place.
flags.action: Stamp every snapshot with the last included game (done in this hub: 'all games through 2026-11-12'), and stop describing it as 'through Week 9'
flags.status: CORRECTED this session - retracted on the evidence in VER-19; keep the as-of stamping rule (S-05)

flags.finding: This session's fresh transcription of the Week 10 report differs from the repo snapshot in exactly one of 345 rows: KC DT Omarr Norman-Lott practice status (repo: Limited participation; live page 2026-11-14: Did not participate). All 345 player identities and game statuses match.
flags.impact: Confirms the injury page mutates between fetches; a snapshot without a timestamp is not reproducible
flags.action: Snapshot per fetch, keep history, diff on every build (VER-03)
flags.status: OPEN - diff automated

flags.finding: The official news roundup headline for Sat 2026-11-14 reads 'Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth (illness) questionable', but the Week 10 injury report table for PIT contains no Freiermuth row (8 rows, none with a game status).
flags.impact: Two official NFL surfaces disagree on a designation; a starter-level prop market (TE receptions/yards) would be priced off the wrong assumption
flags.action: Exclude Freiermuth from all hub signals, leave his row blank, re-check the final Friday report
flags.status: OPEN - excluded and flagged

flags.finding: Two official NFL pages give different absence windows for the same injury: 'Ravens' Lamar Jackson (right thumb) out 6-9 weeks' vs 'Ravens confirm Lamar Jackson expected to miss 6-10 weeks'.
flags.impact: Return-window inputs feed futures and rest-of-season props; a range cannot be treated as a point estimate
flags.action: Store both windows as a range with both citations; never use a midpoint
flags.status: OPEN - range stored, no midpoint used

flags.finding: Baltimore's Week 10 report lists 8 players and no quarterback, while the starter (Jackson, IR per SRC-08) and the reported season-ending backup (Huntley) are both absent. No official page fetched this session identifies the starting QB for LAC@BAL on 2026-11-16.
flags.impact: The single highest-leverage lineup fact for a Monday prime-time game is unknown; every BAL line is unsafe to originate
flags.action: Owner decision Q-06: accept club/inactives as the only source for starters, or skip games with unknown QB
flags.status: OPEN - BAL row published with blank starter, UNVERIFIED

flags.finding: The NFL does not publish betting lines or player-prop prices on any official NFL.com property, so every 'market' column in this hub is intentionally blank. A prior session's market columns came from ESPN/DraftKings (SRC-13), which this session did not fetch and cannot attest to.
flags.impact: No closing line, no CLV, no ROI, and therefore no legitimate leaderboard promotion of any strategy
flags.action: Q-01/S-04: license or hand-record a price archive before any performance claim
flags.status: OPEN - all market cells blank by policy, not by omission

flags.finding: Still true in the strict sense - the league publishes no depth chart - but a usable overlay now exists inside this repository: the desk capture holds 32 club charts and joins them to the injury report (210 rows over weeks 8-10; 76 for Week 10). Of those Week-10 rows only 41 name a replacement, 22 have no string rank at all, 76 of 76 carry no as-of date, and 50 come from charts the club itself labels unofficial.
flags.impact: The literal request 'which 2nd/3rd/4th-stringer replaces the starter' is now answerable for about half the cases, but only from club-published material - never as a certified fact.
flags.action: Render it as a labelled UNVERIFIED overlay beside the certified availability layer (implemented on the depth page), keep it out of any model input or gate evidence.
flags.status: OPEN - overlay published on hub/deficiency.html, badged UNVERIFIED; model inputs still use the official report only

flags.finding: Rows were transcribed from the live official page exactly as printed, including player-club pairings that this session could not cross-check against a verified roster page (no roster page was fetched).
flags.impact: If the source page itself mis-assigns a player to a club, the hub reproduces it
flags.action: Add a roster join (club roster page per team) to the ingestion contract (S-07)
flags.status: OPEN - no row altered, none independently confirmed

flags.finding: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` still triggers on `push` to the merged branch `arena/1a771fcd-x3`, runs five checkers belonging to five different sessions over eight site trees, and branch `arena/64164906-x3` has 5 consecutive failing `data-pipeline` runs (last seen 2026-11-14, 14h ago). PR #12 from another session is still OPEN.

flags.action: S-14/S-15: scope triggers to `main` + PRs, make hub checks the required status, keep other checkers as non-blocking advisories

flags.finding: The injury-report cadence (Wed/Thu/Fri 4 pm ET filings; Out/Doubtful/Questionable; inactives ~90 min before kickoff) is described here from a secondary reference (SRC-12). The league rulebook text was not fetched, so the wording is not certified.

flags.finding: Originated lines here are produced with uncalibrated assumption parameters (home-field advantage 2.0 pts, neutral-site 0.0, positional injury weights, 40% total shrinkage) and reproduce neither of the two prior in-repo models exactly. No line in this hub has passed a single validation gate.
flags.impact: Anyone reading the line table as an edge would be mistaking a formula for skill
flags.action: Keep every model row badged DERIVED, gate G-0..G-9 blocking, leaderboard empty
flags.status: OPEN by design

flags.finding: A prior session published correlations of +0.6984 / -0.6636 / +0.8781 / +0.3501 from the official standings. Recomputing from this session's snapshot gives +0.7001 / -0.6639 / +0.8794 / +0.3506 with games = W+L+T (+0.6943 / -0.6509 / +0.8779 / +0.3506 with ties excluded). Neither denominator convention reproduces the published figures.
flags.evidence: https://github.com/karagemop466-tech/X3/blob/main/dashboard/data/correlations.json vs recomputation in scripts/check_hub.py from hub/data/standings_2026.csv
flags.impact: Small but real: it proves the earlier numbers came from a different standings snapshot, so cross-page comparisons are not like-for-like
flags.action: Cite the snapshot with every derived statistic (VER-05). Extended this session: the published set was tested against four candidate inputs (this hub's standings, the desk game log through W9, and the same log with and without the Week-10 Thursday game, with ties in and out of the denominators) and no variant reproduces it, so the figures cannot be reconstructed from any dataset currently in the repository.
flags.status: RESOLVED for the hub (values recomputed, inputs and formula printed); the prior figures remain unexplained rather than wrong

flags.finding: The Week 10 report used here is the practice/game-status table available on Saturday 2026-11-14 18:08 UTC; Sunday inactives (the final lineup truth) did not exist at fetch time, and the Monday-night game had one more report due.
flags.impact: Questionable-heavy clubs (NYJ 8, NE 9, SF 7, GB 7) may look far stronger or weaker on Sunday than the Saturday table implies

flags.finding: A prior tree's standings table records Tampa Bay's division record as 1-2-0. The official page shows 2-0-0, and the .1000 division percentage printed in the same row is only consistent with 2-0-0. That row feeds that tree's derived numbers.
flags.impact: Any model or table in that tree that uses division record is wrong for TB; found only by re-deriving from the official page
flags.action: Owner: accept the corrected value (this hub uses 2-0-0) and open a fix PR against that tree, or retire it per S-01
flags.status: OPEN - still live on main after the 2026-11-14 integration merge: docs/data/standings-2026-week10.csv was corrected to 2-0-0 by that session, dashboard/data/standings.json was not touched and still reads 1-2-0

flags.finding: Team codes differ between trees: the Rams appear as LA and LAR, the Cardinals as ARI and AZ. The official page renders the Rams logo as logos/LA while using LAR elsewhere, so a naive join across trees silently drops two clubs.
flags.evidence: https://www.nfl.com/standings/league/2026/REG ; prior tree files in dashboard/ and x3lab/
flags.impact: Cross-tree comparisons and any automated merge of prior data mismatch on 2 of 32 clubs. Demonstrated cost: the first run of this session's reconciliation against the desk game log reported 18 false mismatches until LA->LAR and ARI->AZ were aliased; with aliases applied the two independent captures agree on every field for all 32 clubs (VER-19).
flags.action: Freeze one id list (the 32 codes in hub/data/standings_2026.csv) and add an alias map (S-03, Q-18)
flags.status: OPEN

flags.finding: The hub's four computed correlations use 32 team-seasons from a 9-week sample. They describe the relationship between scoring and winning in 2026 to date; they are not evidence of a betting edge.
flags.impact: Readers may mistake a descriptive statistic for a tradable signal
flags.action: Labelled on the page; keep out of any strategy promotion
flags.status: OPEN by design

flags.finding: The prior model table in dashboard/data/model_lines.json publishes a 'model_home_spread' that follows neither the betting convention nor its own expected scores: all 14 rows carry the sign of (exp_home - exp_away) instead of its negation, and 12 of 14 are exactly twice that margin (the other 2 within 0.2). Example, KC at ATL: expected margin -5.6, i.e. the home club is a 5.6-point dog, yet the column reads -11.3, which in betting notation means an 11.3-point home favourite.
flags.evidence: https://github.com/karagemop466-tech/X3/blob/main/dashboard/data/model_lines.json ; recomputed row by row in this session
flags.impact: anyone copying that column slips the wrong side of every game, and the magnitudes are not comparable with a market line
flags.action: the hub states its convention in the table header (negative = home favourite) and shows both prior models side by side so the disagreement is visible
flags.status: OPEN for the legacy trees (not edited here); documented and corrected in the hub

flags.finding: The desk unit publishes r = -0.161 for the pair 'game total vs |margin|' with the reading 'same-game total and blowout size move together'. Recomputing from that unit's own 137 finals gives r(total, |margin|) = -0.016. The published -0.161 is exactly r(total, signed home-minus-away margin) - a different quantity, whose sign has no blowout interpretation. The companion row (away score vs home score, +0.076) reproduces exactly, so the pipeline is fine and the label is wrong.
flags.impact: the one game-level correlation that gates parlay leg selection is mislabelled in a merged, live page; a reader would conclude big games are blowouts when the data says nothing of the kind
flags.action: owner: fix the label in that unit (absolute vs signed margin) or republish both; the hub prints both values computed from the log (correlations page)
flags.status: OPEN - reported, not edited in another session's file

flags.finding: The depth overlay is partial in a way that biases it: of 210 joined rows, 102 match cleanly, 41 have no backup listed at that slot, 47 name a player who is not on his own club's chart, 10 matched on name only with a different position, and 7 clubs' charts were not machine-readable in the capture. For Week 10 that leaves 41 of 76 absences with an identified replacement.
flags.impact: absence of a replacement name is not evidence that none exists; the 44 blanks are mostly capture and naming failures, so a naive count of 'backup in' would understate depletion
flags.action: publish the join status per row (done on the depth page) and never compute a deficiency score from the overlay
flags.status: OPEN - documented, overlay marked partial

flags.finding: A merged session documented that 'the authoring sandbox cannot reach nfl.com' and built a GitHub-Actions capture pipeline around that constraint. This session reached the same pages directly from the sandbox (injuries, standings, schedule, game centre) with the fetch tool, and its transcription matches that pipeline's data. Both routes work; the constraint is tool-specific, not environmental.
flags.impact: an assumed constraint that is not real adds CI machinery where a direct fetch would do; conversely the CI route is more reproducible and should be kept for scheduled snapshots
flags.action: keep both: direct fetch for in-session verification, the runner job for scheduled snapshots (S-05)
flags.status: OPEN - noted so the next session does not re-derive the limitation
